speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing pain and swelling in your right knee, as well as pain when urinating, and you have a history of a similar episode in your left ankle. To help narrow down the cause, can you tell me if you have experienced any fever, chills, or fatigue recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your sexual history and the combination of joint pain and urinary symptoms, I need to rule out a sexually transmitted infection. Have you noticed any discharge from your penis or developed a rash on your hands or feet?

speaker: Doctor
text: I see you are feeling anxious, but your symptoms are very specific. You mentioned you have not noticed any discharge or rash, which helps narrow down the possibilities. Given your history of inconsistent condom use, painful urination, and migratory joint swelling, I need to confirm if you have had any recent diarrhea or abdominal pain before these symptoms started?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history reported. Social history: Sexually active with multiple partners, inconsistent condom use.

speaker: Doctor
text:
I understand you haven't had any recent diarrhea, which helps rule out reactive arthritis triggered by gut infections. To confirm the likely diagnosis of gonococcal arthritis, I need to check for signs of infection in your urine and joints. REQUEST TEST: Urine_NAAT_Gonorrhea_Chlamydia
REQUEST TEST: Joint_Fluid_Culture

speaker: Doctor
text: The negative test results for gonorrhea and chlamydia make gonococcal arthritis unlikely. Given your migratory arthritis and urinary symptoms, I suspect reactive arthritis or another inflammatory condition. Do you have any eye pain, redness, or vision changes?

speaker: Patient
text: Experiences anxiety; denies recent flu-like symptoms, denies any known sexually transmitted infections.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Since you deny eye symptoms and recent infections, and gonococcal tests were negative, I need to check for other inflammatory markers. REQUEST TEST: HLA-B27
REQUEST TEST: ESR_CRP

speaker: Doctor
text: The positive HLA-B27 and elevated ESR, combined with your migratory arthritis and urinary symptoms, strongly point toward reactive arthritis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive Arthritis
